purpose: Public, auditable description of a labelled design pool. The label rows themselves live in a private store outside this repository, located by $BINDERSCOUT_BENCHMARK_STORE and verified against labels.sha256 below. This repo is public; publishing outcome labels would be irreversible.

manifest_fields.name: Pool identifier; must equal the containing directory name.
manifest_fields.description: One line: what the designs are.
manifest_fields.source: Provenance — paper, campaign, or assay run that produced the labels.
manifest_fields.n_designs: Row count of the label file. Checked on load; a mismatch is an error.
manifest_fields.label_column: Column in the label file holding the outcome.
manifest_fields.label_meaning: What the values mean, in words. E.g. '1 = measured binder, 0 = measured non-binder'.

labels.sha256: SHA-256 of that file. A mismatch is an error, not a warning: the rows would not be the ones this manifest describes.

manifest_fields.caveats: Optional. Known label-quality problems. For Cao 2022, 73.4% of binder labels are one-sided-Kd and are experimentally indistinguishable from non-binders on Cao's own binary assay.

notes: A manifest missing any required field is refused rather than half-trusted.
list_benchmarks() must work on a machine with no private data — every CI run and every fresh clone.

example_manifest._comment: Copy into Evaluator/benchmarks/<name>/MANIFEST.json and edit. A separate template FILE would be gitignored by the **/*.json rule, so the example lives here.
example_manifest.name: cao2022
example_manifest.caveats: 73.4% of binder labels are one-sided-Kd and are experimentally indistinguishable from non-binders on Cao's own binary assay; macro-AUC rises from 0.56 to 0.73 once they are excluded.

how_to_add_a_pool: 1. Put the label rows in $BINDERSCOUT_BENCHMARK_STORE/<name>/labels.csv -- OUTSIDE this repo.
4. Check: python -c "from binder_comparison import benchmarks as b; print(len(b.load_labels('<name>')))"
